newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Killed Turkish Cypriot buried in quiet funeral.
newsitem.headline: Killed Turkish Cypriot buried in quiet funeral.

text.p: A Turkish Cypriot shot dead by a hooded gunman in the Greek Cypriot south of the divided Mediterranean island was buried at a quiet ceremony on Monday.

Between 30 to 40 people attended the funeral of Can Necip Hakyemez, in the Turkish Cypriot north of the capital Nicosia. Hakyemez, 38, was killed from four bullets fired at close range by a gunman in the southern town of Limassol on Saturday.
His body was handed over to relatives in northern Cyprus by the United Nations.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 after a coup on the island engineered by the military then ruling Greece.

Hakyemez, one of some 300 Turkish Cypriots who live in the south, was arrested by police earlier this year on suspicion of spying on Greek Cypriot army positions but later released for lack of evidence. He was under inquiry for drugs-related offences.
Police have summoned 15 people, Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots, for questioning about the murder.
